title: Bob node children are subprotocols
statement: Let $X,Y,	ext{ and }[0m\alpha$ be types, let $f:Y\to\{0,1\}$, and let $P$ assign a protocol over these types to each bit. For every bit $b$, the child protocol $P(b)$ is a subprotocol of the Bob node determined by $f$ and $P$.
hypotheses_covered: A function from Bob's input type $Y$ to a bit
A protocol-valued function on the two bits
replaced:
Let $f : Y \to \{0,1\}$ be a Bob decision function and let $P$ assign a protocol $P(b)$
to each bit $b$. Then for every bit $b$, the child $P(b)$ is a subprotocol of the Bob
node $\texttt{bob}\; f\; P$.
